The database adapter contract - feature 3 of the feature audit.
This is the list every adapter in every framework must implement, in full.
It is data rather than four hand-maintained interface declarations, because
four declarations are exactly how the frameworks ended up with four different
answers to 'implement the Tina4 adapter interface'.
EVERY METHOD IS REQUIRED. There are no optional members. Node declared
getTableColumns? and addColumn? optional, which forces the facade to
feature-detect at every call site - the same pattern as Ruby's respond_to?
guards, written in TypeScript. An optional method on a contract is not a
contract.
SQL DIALECT TRANSLATION IS NOT HERE, deliberately. Python's adapter base
declares eight translation methods (limit_to_rows, limit_to_top, ...) beside
the connection and CRUD contract, so 'how do I talk to this engine' and 'how
do I rewrite SQL for this dialect' are one abstraction. The other three keep
translation in its own unit. An adapter declares its dialect; the translator
does the rewriting.

methods.name: execute
methods.note: write; RAISES on error, never returns false

methods.name: getTables
methods.note: -> list of table names. NOT tables()

methods.name: getColumns
methods.note: -> list of column descriptors. NOT columns()

methods.name: createTable
methods.note: -> bool. Required: every engine can do it

methods.name: addColumn
methods.note: -> bool. Required: every engine can do it

naming._note: Same concept, same name, idiomatic casing. The table below is the source of truth for what a caller types in each framework.
naming.python: snake_case: open, close, execute, execute_many, fetch, fetch_one, insert, update, delete, start_transaction, commit, rollback, get_tables, get_columns, table_exists, create_table, add_column, last_insert_id, error, autocommit
naming.php: camelCase: open, close, execute, executeMany, fetch, fetchOne, insert, update, delete, startTransaction, commit, rollback, getTables, getColumns, tableExists, createTable, addColumn, lastInsertId, error, autocommit

dropped.query: PHP and Node declare it, Python does not, and nothing in the framework needs a second read path beside fetch/fetchOne. Dropped rather than added to two more frameworks.
dropped.sql_translation: Python's eight dialect methods (limit_to_rows, limit_to_top, concat_pipes_to_func, boolean_to_int, ilike_to_like, placeholder_style, auto_increment_syntax, quote_identifier) move to the SQLTranslator unit that PHP, Ruby and Node already have.

renames.tables -> getTables: node. The majority and the get- prefix convention win.
renames.getTableColumns? -> getColumns: node. It was an optional duplicate of getColumns.
